name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
description: Adversaries send a targeted message with a malicious attachment to gain execution or harvest credentials. Attachments often include Office macros, ISO/LNK loaders, or credential-stealing HTML.
detection: Correlate mail gateway detonations, sandbox verdicts, endpoint process ancestry from Outlook/browser, and newly created persistence shortly after open events.
soc_response: Quarantine the message org-wide, disable the mailbox forwarding rules, isolate endpoints that opened the attachment, reset credentials for users who submitted passwords, and hunt for related payloads by hash and parent/child process.
observables: Suspicious attachment hash or filename (invoice.iso, statement.docm)
Outlook spawning WINWORD/EXCEL then cmd.exe, wscript, or powershell.exe
Impossible travel or MFA fatigue immediately after the email
containment: Block sender domain and attachment hash at the mail gateway. Isolate affected workstations. Do not forward the sample via email; use the malware detonation pipeline.

name: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
description: Adversaries lure users to a credential harvest or malware download site. AiTM kits proxy Microsoft 365 or Okta logons to steal session cookies.
detection: URL rewrite logs, proxy categories, identity protection 'unfamiliar properties', OAuth consent grants, and token replay from rare ASNs.
soc_response: Revoke refresh tokens, force MFA re-registration if AiTM is confirmed, disable risky inbox rules, and search for the same URL/campaign across the tenant.
observables: User agent mismatch after successful auth
New inbox rule: hide from, forward to external
Session from hosting ASN minutes after a click
containment: Block URL at secure web gateway and email. Revoke sessions. Preserve mailbox audit and Entra/Okta sign-in logs.

name: Valid Accounts
tactic: Defense Evasion / Persistence / Privilege Escalation / Initial Access
description: Adversaries use legitimate credentials rather than malware to blend into normal authentication. Common after phishing, infostealers, or password spraying.
detection: Impossible travel, atypical protocol (legacy auth), privileged group changes, and access to high-value mailboxes or cloud resources from new devices.
soc_response: Disable or reset the account, revoke tokens, review group membership deltas, and hunt for mailbox rules, app consents, and lateral authentication.
observables: Access to finance or VIP mailboxes
containment: Disable account, revoke sessions, rotate secrets for any service accounts reused, and block source IP/ASN if still active.

name: Brute Force: Password Spraying
description: A small set of common passwords is tried against many accounts to avoid lockouts. Often precedes valid-account abuse.
detection: Spike in failures across many users from one ASN, followed by a small number of successes. Smart lockout telemetry and IdP risk events.
soc_response: Block source IPs, enable or tighten lockout and MFA, reset successfully guessed accounts, and check whether any mailbox or VPN sessions were established.
observables: High failure rate, low unique passwords
Success after spray against service or dormant accounts
VPN or RDP from the same source
containment: Firewall/IdP block on source. Reset compromised accounts. Disable legacy authentication.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
description: Adversaries use PowerShell for discovery, credential access, download cradles, and in-memory loaders. Encoded commands and bypasses are common.
detection: Script block logging, AMSI events, encoded CommandLine (-enc), download cradles (IEX, DownloadString), and unusual parent processes.
soc_response: Collect ScriptBlock and 4104/4103 events, dump the process command line, isolate the host if C2 is suspected, and hunt the same encoded blob estate-wide.
observables: Office or browser as parent of powershell.exe
containment: Isolate endpoint, kill offending process tree, block the download URL/hash, preserve Memory/EDR timeline.

name: Remote Services: RDP
description: Stolen credentials are used to move via Remote Desktop. Attackers may enable RDP, add users to Remote Desktop Users, or hijack existing sessions.
detection: 4624 type 10 from unusual sources, 4625 bursts, new local admins, and RDP from workstations that never previously sourced interactive logons.
soc_response: Disable the compromised account, isolate source and destination hosts, review the RDP session for staging directories, and check for scheduled tasks created during the session.
observables: RDP from a user workstation to a server jumphost reverse path
containment: Disable RDP from the source, reset credentials, revoke cached credentials, capture disk/EDR evidence before rebuild.

name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
description: C2 over HTTP/HTTPS blends with normal browsing. Beacons may use rare JA3/JA4, long-lived connections, or domain fronting.
detection: Beaconing intervals, rare domains, newly registered domains, TLS to non-standard SNI, and EDR network events from unsigned binaries.
soc_response: Sinkhole or block the domain/IP, isolate the beaconing host, capture the binary and config, and hunt identical mutex/hash/C2 across the fleet.
observables: Periodic HTTPS to a newly registered domain
containment: Network isolate. Block IOC at DNS/proxy/firewall. Do not power off if memory analysis is required; use EDR containment.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Ransomware encrypts files and may destroy backups, inhibit recovery, and drop ransom notes. Often follows privilege escalation and backup tampering.
detection: Mass file rename/entropy, VSS deletion (vssadmin, wbadmin, wmic shadowcopy), ransom notes, and simultaneous encryption across shares.
soc_response: Isolate affected segments, preserve a few encrypted samples and notes, identify patient zero and backup integrity, and engage IR leadership before any payment discussion.
observables: Rapid file extension changes on file servers
containment: Take encrypted systems off the network. Disable the staging account. Snapshot clean backups offline. Do not power-cycle all hosts blindly.

name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
description: Data leaves over DNS, FTP, ICMP, or cloud storage APIs instead of the primary C2 channel. Often paired with archive and encrypt staging.
detection: Large outbound transfers, DNS TXT spikes, unsanctioned cloud sync, and archive creation in temp followed by network egress.
soc_response: Block the egress channel, identify the staged archive, estimate data types involved, and notify legal/privacy if regulated data may have left.
containment: Egress block on the host and destination. Preserve staging directories. Capture packet or proxy logs covering the transfer window.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Internet-facing services (VPN, web apps, file transfer) are exploited for unauthenticated RCE or auth bypass, frequently used as ransomware footholds.
detection: WAF/IDS signatures, anomalous request paths, webshell drops under web roots, and new child processes of w3wp/nginx/httpd.
soc_response: Take the vulnerable service offline or patch/WAF virtual-patch, hunt webshells and persistence, rotate secrets stored on the host, and review downstream lateral movement.
observables: Web shell files in /uploads or inetpub
Scanner user-agents hitting a new CVE path
containment: Block exploit path at WAF/VPN. Isolate the server. Preserve web logs and the web root before cleanup.

name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
description: Adversaries create or modify scheduled tasks to maintain access, often under SYSTEM or a privileged user.
detection: Event 4698/4702, schtasks.exe, Task Scheduler operational log, and tasks pointing to user-writable paths.
soc_response: Export the task XML, hash the action binary, disable the task, and hunt the same task name across endpoints.
observables: Recently created task with random name
containment: Disable the task, isolate if C2 is confirmed, collect the action binary and XML.

name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
description: Adversaries dump LSASS to recover credentials for lateral movement. Tools include Mimikatz-style loaders, comsvcs MiniDump, and direct syscalls.
detection: LSASS handle access (Sysmon 10), MiniDump from unusual processes, Credential Guard bypass attempts, and subsequent authentications with stolen hashes.
soc_response: Isolate the host, rotate credentials for accounts that authenticated to it, assume NTLM hashes are burned, and hunt for follow-on PtH/PtT.
containment: Isolate. Reset affected accounts including krbtgt if domain-wide dump is suspected (coordinate with AD owners). Enable Credential Guard where missing.
